body.statement: Does the conditional endpoint-mixture causal-completion handle establish the following exhaustive extension property? For every \(a\in\mathcal A_Y(\mu)\), every observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying the support and overlap conditions, and a corresponding \(\beta\in\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)\) with \(a=\mu-B^{\mathsf T}\beta\), construct one joint law \(P\in\mathfrak M(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) of \(G\) and all \(\{Y_t(p^r):t\in\mathcal T,r\in\mathcal R\}\) that preserves the entire joint distribution of \(O\), realizes the same \(a\) and \(\beta\), satisfies consistency along the realized complete path \(p^G\), and simultaneously defines every \(\theta_j=E_P[Y_{t_j}(p^{g_j})-Y_{t_j}(p^\infty)\mid G=g_j]=\nu_j-s_j^{\mathsf T}\beta\) for \(j\in\mathcal J\). The worked diagnostic requires, in particular, deciding whether \(\mathsf{Comp}_3(z)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(z\in[-1,1/2]\). If the general property fails, characterize the smallest additional cross-path compatibility inequality and a minimal graph counterexample.
body.justification: Mean feasibility is not causal sharpness until every feasible mean vector is lifted to one common bounded full-data law indexed by fully specified announcement-and-implementation paths.
body.gap: Torgovitsky2019 proves sharpness by extending lower-dimensional distributional objects, and PiccininniTchetgenStensrud2025 shows why the intervention being anticipated must be explicit. Neither paper supplies a staggered completion over one known canonical path per implementation cohort with overlapping comparison cohorts.
body.consumer: A positive resolution makes every reported endpoint an attainable announced-policy ATT, while a negative resolution supplies the missing restriction needed by all bounded-anticipation risk-set analyses.
